Overview

Template MINIO_Vendor_Template_10192026.xlsx from SOA: 61 columns, tabs Field Restrictions, Vendor Template, Vendor Category
Required Company Name (marked red). First and Last Name are required instead when the vendor is an individual
Source of truth Sage Intacct vendor detail export, 1,770 active vendors
Enrichment Ramp vendor export, 578 vendors. 551 carry the Sage vendor ID, so the link is exact
Not loaded Bank details (ACH and wire). The template has no bank fields
Status Scope and rules agreed 2026-10-26. Load plan and remaining questions below

Column mapping

Same approach as the customer load: Sage first, Ramp fills gaps, rules marked as rules.

Added columns

Not in the template, kept as on the customer load. Source IDs, as custom fields: Sage Vendor ID (as in Sage, also in the template’s Legacy Vendor ID) and Ramp Vendor ID. For review only: Question Categories, Duplicate Action, Ramp Category, Owner, Department, Last activity (latest of Sage last bill, Sage last payment, Ramp last spend), Ramp 365-day spend, Flags.

The export of all active vendors lists 1,775. The 5 not in the detail export are flagged One-time use in Sage. The Sage vendor list report has 1,788: the 1,775 plus 13 inactive.

Load plan

Agreed 2026-10-26: every active Sage vendor ends up in NetSuite, with Ramp syncing its vendors.

  1. Ramp sync. Ramp syncs its 578 vendors to NetSuite, including the 27 Ramp vendors not in Sage (added in Ramp from 2025-08 on, 23 with no spend yet).
  2. Sage vendors not in Ramp. This load: the 1,219 active Sage vendors that are not in Ramp, mapped as above.
  3. Enrichment. The 551 vendors in both systems get Sage values Ramp does not hold: Sage Vendor ID, Vendor Category, default expense account, 1099 flag, tax ID where Ramp has none, and bank details where Ramp has none.

Open questions

  1. Order of Ramp sync and load. Ramp’s NetSuite sync works both ways: it can import existing NetSuite vendors and link Ramp merchants to them. Loading all 1,770 Sage vendors first and then connecting Ramp avoids two problems with syncing first: Ramp-created vendors carry no Sage ID, so the enrichment step has to match by name, and Ramp names that already exist in NetSuite raise duplicate-name errors. Which order does SOA recommend?
  2. Subsidiary for INR and SGD vendors. Ramp supports several entities mapped to NetSuite subsidiaries, but Ramp’s export shows only MinIO, Inc. as a default entity (79 vendors, the rest blank). Vendors to look up: INR: V-01301 TDS Tax Payable, V-01311 Universal Actuaries and Benefit Consultants, V-01352 and V-01353 Zoho Corporation Private Limited, V-01354 91 Springboard Business Hub Private Limited, V-01380 Resurgent India Limited, V-01381 National Securities Depository Limited, V-01412 S P Nagarajan, V-01459 Vishnu Daya & Co LLP. SGD: V-00628 Cloud Expo Asia Pte. Ltd. Also GBP: V-00629 Reed Exhibitions Ltd. Several INR vendors have United States as their Sage country.
  3. Bank details import. SOA to provide the template for vendor bank details, and confirm whether Ramp syncs bank details to NetSuite.
  4. Five bank accounts differ between Sage and Ramp. Ramp is assumed current; confirm.
